# holtburger-web 1070 perf campaign — 2026-10-06

Rig: GTX 1070 box, Chrome 154 (fresh profile, off-screen, muted, `--use-angle=d3d11`),
1280x633 canvas, `quality=mid` (the 1070's auto-detected preset), `adaptiveRes=off`,
`skytime=12`, Holtburg `@teleloc 0xA9B40001 96 96 80`, camera orbit 70 m / el 22 deg / 12 deg/s.
Drivers (scratchpad): `hbprobe.mjs` (fresh-boot attribution: census + CPU profile + GPU util),
`hbsess.mjs` (persistent session: boot/eval/snap/profile), `abwin.js` (interleaved in-session A/B).

## Baseline (HEAD 355f1eb9)
- ~23 fps, p50 41.7 ms, 1% low 13.3 fps. GPU util 22% => main-thread bound.
- ~2,000 draws/frame; three.js submission ~24 ms/frame (renderBufferDirect), setProgram 37% of all CPU.
- 950 material switches + 221 program switches per frame.
- Draw census: entity part meshes 814 (593 unique materials, ~40/humanoid NPC), cellstatic 480,
  surfaces-fused (interiors) 190, static particles ~250 (one Mesh + cloned material each),
  static-batch-c 167 (31 us/draw, 66 program switches over 13 programs).
- updateMatrixWorld 3.1 ms + projectObject 2.9 ms (7,776 nodes), tickPerFrame 4 ms.

## Found: black frame (the 10-05 NanScrub fix never worked)
- 2 NaN pixels from one interior cell material (surfaces-fused-opaque-a9b40147, group 1) => bloom
  smeared NaN over the whole frame => whole 3D view black on the 1070.
- Cause 1: Effect default blend NORMAL = mix(dst, src, 1) => NaN*0 = NaN, scrubbed pixel re-NaN'd.
- Cause 2: isnan() folded away by the D3D compile. Fix: SRC blend + exponent-bit test + clamp >= 0.
- Verified live: frame renders (mean 1.7 -> 107).

## Fix 1: program sort restored under ?punchRetail
- punchRetail's setOpaqueSort ran after installDrawSortProgram and replaced it. Phase is now the
  primary key inside the program sort.
- Program switches 246.6 -> 126.6 /frame. fps 23.7 -> 24.7, 1% low 13.8 -> 16.4.

## Fix 2: ?occlusionCull (GPU occlusion queries, interiors + entity rigs)
- Upper bound measured first: doorway-cells-only + indoor NPCs hidden = 24.5 -> 30.5 fps.
- Live A/B (4 reps x 6 s interleaved): 24.6 -> 28.1 fps, p50 41.6 -> 33.4 ms, 1% low 13.8 -> 19.0.
- Content draws ~1,630 -> ~1,140 (+~170 proxy draws). Snapshot diff on/off: only animation.

## Fix 4: ?asyncLink (scene3d/async_link_guard.js)
- Draws of the main scene whose material has no program / a still-linking program / a version we
  have not compiled are SKIPPED and compiled off-frame (one compile() per drain via a duck-typed root,
  a cached-lights stand-in target scene; per-material KHR_parallel_shader_compile readiness polls).
- Single cold Shoushi tours: max hitch 1,700 -> 708-850 ms; 1% low 3.5 -> 5.0 fps; 0.1% low 0.7 -> 2.1 fps.
  3x3 rep bench pending.

## Session 2 (17:06-18:31 NDT) — eye-test + tune of the default-on changes (owner: keep all ON)
Live 1070 session (fresh profile, mid, Holtburg). In-page probes, no reboots between before/after
except the one to load the fixes.

**asyncLink — static-atlas blink (FIXED).** Per-material skip spans across a cold Holtburg→Shoushi
teleport: the two transparent atlas buckets (`stat-atlas-x-8x8|1|…`, `stat-atlas-x-1024x1024|1|…`,
most of the town's statics) were skipped on 107 separate frames spread over 23.4 s. Cause: three r184
draws a transparent DoubleSide material in two passes, each preceded by `side = Back|Front;
needsUpdate = true`, so `version` moves twice per frame (~17,000 after a few minutes); the guard's
rate cap let 2 deferrals through per 2 s window ⇒ a 1-frame blink every ~2 s. Fix: a version-move
compile that added no program to the material's `programs` map is a no-op; after 2 in a row the
material's version moves draw through; a trusted draw that does build a program revokes the trust
(`stats.trustRevoked`). After: atlas buckets absent from the skip list, longest skip span 23.4 → 5.6 s,
compile drains 693 → 370, compiles 2,546 → 2,100, trustRevoked 0. Cold Yaraq tour: remaining skips are
first links only (neverDrawn 194 / noProgram 184 / inFlight 425 skip-draws; real version moves 35 over
23 materials). Only these 2 meshes use three's two-pass at Holtburg (census), so no wider perf lead.

**occlusionCull — pop-in.** Reveal probe (patched `beginFrame`, 3rd-person sweeps 8 m/12 s, 8 m/4 s,
4 m/2 turns): every hidden→visible reveal lands 1-2 frames late (p50 1, max 2 — the query minimum).
Still camera: 0 false reveals. One cell (0xA9B40176, ~70 m) re-revealed over and over while the
camera moved (edge grazing). Fix: a proxy re-revealed within 90 frames doubles its hide delay
(3→6→12→24); a quiet one starts over. Sweeps after (before): big reveals 32/15/22 (43/17/27), hidden
proxies per frame 71/83/83 (72/91/83, culling unchanged), fps 37/44/45 (37/38/43).
Street-level on/off snap pairs at 4 headings: differences only on animated things (rotating crystal,
swaying trees, player idle, birds) — nothing missing with culling on.

**particleInstancingAlpha — draw order.** Holtburg alpha particles are ~all one gfxobj (0x1000fbf
chimney smoke), sorted back-to-front inside its bucket each tick; additive buckets write no depth
(order-independent). Residual: the static and world particle managers each own a 0x1000fbf alpha
bucket; buckets sit at the identity origin, so three orders them by that origin, not by content —
where two plumes from different managers overlap on screen, the one drawn second can be clipped by
the first one's alphaTest depth writes. Not changed (rare; a fix = one shared alpha bucket per gfxobj
across managers, or a per-tick centroid offset).

**Remaining async-link pop-in after a cold teleport** is the intended trade: first-link objects are
missing for up to ~3 s (static-batch-c 0x0800049e: 66 skipped frames over 3.3 s at Shoushi) instead of
a 1-2 s freeze.

## Session 2b (17:30-17:55 NDT) — the NaN interior material, fixed at its source
Booted with `?nanScrub=off` so the NaN shows again (orbit pose frame mean 2 = black; hiding
`surfaces-fused-opaque-a9b40147` → 106). Group 1 (surface 0x08000371) geometry is clean: no
non-finite or zero-length normals, no degenerate triangles or UVs, `acBakedLight` in [0, 0.98].
Material bisect with `__asyncLink.off = true` (else a new program is SKIPPED, not drawn — a
fresh-material swap looked like a fix but was just a skipped draw): dropping normal / roughness / AO
maps or DoubleSide changes nothing; dropping the RND-04 vertex-bake patch fixes it; inside the patch,
the direct-term `*= 0` is innocent (keep-direct and select-zero variants still black); clamping the
sRGB decode input fixes it (106), as does skipping the decode.
Cause: `acBakedEotf` = `mix(pow((c + 0.055) / 1.055, 2.4), c / 12.92, step(c, 0.04045))`; the
interpolated varying lands a hair below 0 on a few samples, pow() of a negative base is NaN, and mix()
keeps the NaN even where step() selects the linear branch. Fix: `c = clamp(c, 0.0, 1.0)` first
(materials.js; exact for every in-range value). After (default build): 0 non-finite pixels entering
NanScrub at the orbit pose and at street level (20 frames each). NanScrub stays as the safety net.

**Measurement trap found on the way (also fixed): three r184 `readRenderTargetPixelsAsync` leaves its
PIXEL_PACK_BUFFER bound while it awaits the fence.** The far-fog probe (its only caller) issues one
every 12 frames; for the rest of that frame every synchronous `readPixels` into an array fails with
INVALID_OPERATION and returns zeros. Every frame-readback probe (incl. earlier sessions') read those
frames as pure black: 6-8 "black frames" per 91 at every pose, uniforms finite, scene buffer NaN-free.
Fix: loop.js unbinds right after the call (three re-binds its own buffer before getBufferSubData).
After: 0/91 at orbit, 3 street headings, released camera. Probe rule: check `gl.getError()` after a
readPixels before believing a black read.

## Session 2c (18:05-18:12 NDT) — first-turn hitch: GPU-process trace (lead, no code change)
Full-browser Chrome trace (playwright `browser.startTracing`, categories toplevel, gpu, viz,
disabled-by-default-gpu.service/decoder, devtools.timeline, v8.execute, cc) across the FIRST
3rd-person 360° street sweep after a fresh boot (12 s). Parsers: session scratchpad
`gputrace.mjs` / `gpuattr*.py` (trace kept at /mnt/wbterminal1/tmp/claude-scratch/perf/firstturn-trace*.json).
- Every long main-thread frame (177-654 ms, 12 in 12 s) = TimerFire → RunMicrotasks →
  `CommandBufferHelper::Finish` / `WaitForGetOffset`: three r184 `readRenderTargetPixelsAsync`'s 4 ms
  poll timer resolving, then `getBufferSubData` — a synchronous command-buffer round-trip that waits
  for the GPU process to drain its WHOLE WebGL backlog. The caller is the far-fog probe (4 Hz).
- GPU process in those windows: CrGpuMain ~100% busy in `WebGL` / `CommandBuffer::Flush` slices of
  up to 17-19 ms (ANGLE/D3D11 executing the renderer's queued commands).
- A/B `?farFogSkyHz=0.1` (fresh boot, same sweep): long Finish waits 12 → 1, but worst frames are
  unchanged (617/458/417/375/367 ms vs 408/408/358/358/350; 43 vs 48 frames). The probe is only WHERE
  the main thread absorbs the GPU-process backlog; the bottleneck is the GPU process itself.
- Caveat: gpu.service tracing inflates GPU-process cost (≈4 fps traced vs 35-42 untraced) — read the
  above as attribution, not timing.
Next: attribute the GPU-process backlog by command type (texture uploads vs draw submission vs
compiles) with lighter categories, and an UNTRACED fresh-boot A/B of `farFogSkyHz` on frame timing.
